reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's Hundred-Wit, Thousand-Wit, and Single-Wit (Book V) and the frame on The Lion-Makers; the frame is stated correctly: the wheel-bearer tells this tale to the gold-finder.
The plot follows Ryder: the warning at sunset, both fish's boasts, the frog and its wife leaving that night, the dawn netting, the two fish's deaths and the frog's mocking chant.

Age band 12+: the clever fish are friends, not villains, and every creature in the pond is netted; the deaths are one calm sentence and 'hangs limp and dead' is softened, disclosed. The content note says so plainly.
Ryder's moral that fate outweighs intelligence is put to readers as a discussion question; the added decisiveness moral is disclosed. The pause question comes before the frog decides; no em dashes.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, under 650 KB; seams measured at x=512 and y=512/1024; painted to every edge with no text. One gpt-5.6-sol generation, no edits.
The silver fish, the golden fish and the green frog are consistent; the frog's wife appears only in panels 4 and 6. The two fishermen are consistent and have no caste markers.
Panel 5 shows both fish alive beside the net; panel 6 shows only a covered basket and a bag as the fishermen walk away, with the frogs safe in a stone trough. No dead fish appear anywhere.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children or parents.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.

Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol (gpt-6.1-sol is not available to this account) and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels, not in the app in dark mode.
